docs.title: AIDDbot Glossary
docs.html:
AIDDbot Glossary

The shared language of AIDDbot. People, agents, documents, and code use these terms with these meanings. This page is the single source of truth for them.

How to use this glossary

  • Use the term exactly as written here.
  • Avoid marks words that cause real confusion. Do not use them for the same concept.
  • Write a code identifier in backticks, such as spec.
  • Link to a term with its anchor, such as glossary.md#spec.
  • Add or change a term here first. Then update the documents that use it.
  • Add a term when two or more documents use it, or when people confuse it with another term.

Terms

TermDefinitionCode
AIDDbotA framework of reusable skills, document templates, and scripts for AI-assisted software development. Intent—
PersonA human who works on a project: writes specs, reviews changes, and gives human approval. Avoid: user. A user is the end user of the software.—
AgentAn AI model that works in an AI coding tool. It follows skills and project context, and it calls scripts.—
AI coding toolAn application that runs an agent on a project, such as Codex, Claude Code, or Cursor. Shared core—
DogfoodingTesting AIDDbot on AIDDbot. This repository uses each skill, template, and script as soon as it exists. Rules—
SkillInstructions for a recurring development activity: objective, required context, expected outputs, and checks. The agent chooses the approach. Building blocksSKILL.md
ScriptA command that does one deterministic task with defined inputs, outputs, and errors. Skills call it. Avoid: tool, helper. Script contractaiddbot <group> <action>
AIDDbot CLIThe single executable that ships all scripts as subcommands. Skills call a pinned version. Command formaiddbot
InstallerThe program that installs and updates a pinned AIDDbot release in a project: skills, templates, and CLI. Avoid: script, for the installer. H4—
RepositoryA Git repository. The official Git term.—
ProjectA repository seen as a place of work: its AGENTS.md, specs, wiki, and roadmap. AIDDbot installs in a project. A monorepo is one project. Avoid: project, for a part of a monorepo (as Nx and .NET use it).—
PackageA unit of code in a project that is built and versioned on its own, such as an npm package or a part of a monorepo. Avoid: module, for this concept.packages/
ProductWhat the software does or should do for its users, and the value it gives them. One or more systems deliver it.—
SystemSoftware with observable behavior: it takes inputs and gives responses. It can be a whole product, a service, a CLI, or a component. Packages from one or more repositories build it.<system> in EARS
Project contextThe conventions, commands, and constraints of a project that agents read before they work.AGENTS.md
ChangeOne unit of work that goes from a spec to a merge. It has one change type and one spec. Change flow—
Change typeThe category of a change. It matches the Conventional Commits type and guides the requirements. An epic only groups specs. Change typeschore, refactor, fix, feat
Impact levelHow much process a change needs: small, medium, or large. A skill proposes it from criteria, and a person confirms it. It is independent of the change type. Avoid: level (alone), size. Impact levelsimpact
Change flowThe five steps of every change: Analysis, Design, Implementation, Verification, and Close. It is the work of the Development phase. A step is change level. Change flow—
Lifecycle phaseOne of the four phases of the project loop: Foundation, Development, Release, Maintenance. A phase is project level. Avoid: stage; phase, for a step of a change. Lifecycle phases—
DevelopmentThe lifecycle phase that holds the changes. Each change follows the change flow. Change flow—
Project brainThe LIVE project documents with Form DOC, such as the glossary, the wiki pages, and the roadmap. The knowledge wiki is one part of it. It sits between the project loop and the change loop. Foundation creates the first ones. Each change reads them in Analysis and Design, and Close updates them. Lifecycle phases—
Project levelWork on the whole project: the lifecycle phases, such as Foundation or a release. Lifecycle phases—
Change levelWork on one change, from its spec to its close: the steps of the change flow. Lifecycle phases—
ProblemWhat must be solved, in the domain language. The problem space of DDD: domain and subdomains. Analysis works on it, in each change.—
SolutionHow the software solves the problem. The solution space of DDD: bounded contexts, model, and code. Design and Implementation build it. Avoid: solution, for a .NET solution file.—
VerificationThe evidence that the solution solves the problem. Also the change step that checks the requirements.Spec section
CloseThe last step of a change: freeze the spec, harvest the knowledge into the project brain, and add an entry to the Unreleased section of the changelog. It is not a lifecycle phase. Release reads the entries of many closed changes. Close a change—
Spec-firstEvery change starts with a spec. The spec drives the change and is frozen when it closes. Living documents keep the knowledge afterwards. Principles—
SpecThe change document with the problem, solution, and verification of one change. A person approves it before any code, or in the pull request for a small change. Specspec
User storyA need of a role, in the USERSTORY form As a <role>, I want <action>, so that <benefit>. A spec has 1 to 3, coded US1 to US3. SpecSpec section
RequirementOne observable outcome that a change must produce, written in EARS and linked to one user story. A checkbox in the spec marks it as verified. A spec has up to 9. Each one is coded inside its user story, such as US1R2; from another document, s0002-US1R2. Avoid: acceptance criterion. SpecSpec section
ScenarioOne example of a requirement, in GHERKIN steps: Given, When, Then. It has the full requirement code as a tag, such as @s0002-US1R2. End-to-end tests run it. SpecScenario
Feature fileA Gherkin file with the scenarios of one user story, in the spec folder, such as s0002-US1.feature. Analysis writes it, with declarative scenarios. A person approves it with the spec. Implementation generates the end-to-end tests from it. Document catalogfeature-file
Domain modelThe living document of the bounded contexts, aggregates, and entities of a project, with their relations in a Mermaid erDiagram. A spec shows only the data model that its change touches. Document catalogdomain-model
TaskOne step of a change, small enough to verify on its own. Tasks are a checklist in the spec.Spec section
ReviewA check of the diff of a change against the review gates, by an agent or a person. It decides pass or changes needed. It is part of the Verification step. Avoid: review (alone) for the wiki review. Say "wiki review".review-report (when separate)
CheckAn action that verifies a result: a test, a linter, a type check, or a manual review step.—
Quality checkA deterministic check that runs in Implementation: build, format, lint, or unit tests. Foundation sets up their commands in agents. Quality checks—
End-to-end testA test that checks the system from outside, generated from a feature file. It keeps the scenario tags. Another agent instance writes it, in its own package, without reading the source code. Independent end-to-end testse2e-test
Test reportThe result of one run of the end-to-end tests: pass or fail for each scenario, grouped by requirement tag. Verification writes it. Git does not keep it.test-report
Check reportThe result of one run of the quality checks, with each error and its place in the code. The agent reads it to fix the code. The last one goes to Verification. Git does not keep it. Quality checkscheck-report
Review gateOne area that the agent review checks on the diff. It gives pass or changes needed. The defaults are security, user experience, and maintainability. A project configures its gates in agents. Review gates—
EvidenceThe output that shows a check ran and what it found: a test result, a log excerpt, a screenshot, or a link. Inclusion criteria—
FindingA problem, gap, or lesson found during a change. Process findings improve the way of working.review-report
Human approvalA decision that a person must take before the agent continues. Skills mark these decisions and show the evidence. Inclusion criteria—
Living documentA document maintained for the whole life of a project. LifeLIVE
Change documentA document written for one change. When the change closes, its status becomes done and nobody edits it again. LifeCHG
MetadataThe YAML frontmatter at the start of every document: id, type, title, status, created, updated, and links. A spec also has change, its change type, and impact, its impact level. The id is unique. MetadataMETA
ADRArchitecture decision record. A living document for one significant, hard-to-reverse decision. A new ADR supersedes it; nobody edits it.adr
ChangelogThe versioned history of notable changes, in CHANGELOG.md. Avoid: log (alone).changelog
Knowledge wikiThe linked Markdown pages in docs/wiki/ that hold what a project knows now: a second brain for all the project documentation. Agents maintain it from sources. Avoid: brain, second brain (as a term). Wiki modeldocs/wiki/
Knowledge explorerA static web site that tells the story of AIDDbot to people: a map of the method, one page for each element, and the full documents. It reads the AIDDbot documents and never edits them. It does not ship. Explorer developmentpackages/explorer/
Wiki pageOne page of the knowledge wiki, about one topic. Avoid: note, doc. Page ruleswiki-page
SourceAn original input that the wiki cites and never edits, such as a closed spec, a review report, an ADR, an issue, a pull request, or a raw file. Sources—
HarvestMoving durable knowledge from a closed change to the living documents that it affects. For wiki pages, the harvest is an ingest. Principles—

docs.title: AIDDbot Project Intent
docs.html:
AIDDbot Project Intent

Purpose

AIDDbot is a reusable framework of skills and scripts for AI-assisted software development. It helps teams:

  • coordinate AI work across the whole lifecycle,
  • apply their own standards and engineering practices,
  • keep decisions, progress, and verification visible.

It works with any project type or stack. It works with AI coding tools that read AGENTS.md and Agent Skills, such as Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor.

Origin

Alberto Basalo created AIDDbot. He uses it as a proof of concept for his courses at AI Code Academy.

Engineering foundations

Teams pick the practices that fit their project. Skills and templates build on:

  • Extreme Programming (XP): small verifiable changes, short feedback loops, continuous integration, regular refactoring.
  • Domain-Driven Design (DDD): one shared domain language in talk, docs, and code; bounded contexts where needed.
  • Clean Architecture: business rules independent of frameworks and infrastructure; dependencies point to the core.
  • Testing: TDD where it clarifies behavior; test level chosen by risk; a regression test for every defect.

Lifecycle phases

AIDDbot covers four lifecycle phases. Each phase has a one-word name. Work happens in two loops:

  • Project loop: the four phases of the whole project. They are project level.
  • Change loop: the five steps of one change, inside Development. They are change level. See the change flow.
#PhaseWorkUsesProduces
0FoundationPrepare the project set, its quality checks and review gates, and the knowledge wiki.—agents, readme, glossary, wiki-page
1DevelopmentDeliver the changes, one at a time. Each change follows the change flow: Analysis, Design, Implementation, Verification, and Close.——
2ReleaseGroup the closed changes into one version. Turn the Unreleased section of the changelog into the version, check readiness, and support deploy and rollback.changelogchangelog
3MaintenanceInvestigate incidents, update dependencies, and turn recurring issues into new changes.——
  • Uses and Produces hold document IDs from the document catalog, in backticks. Other text is plain. The documents of one change are in the change flow only.
  • Phase and step. A phase is project level. A step is change level. Each name is used once.
  • Project brain. The LIVE project documents form the project brain. Foundation creates the first ones. Each change reads them in Analysis and Design. Close updates them.
  • From Close to Release. Close writes an entry in the Unreleased section of the changelog. Many changes close before one release. Release reads the changelog and makes the version.
  • Problem, solution, verification. Analysis works on the problem. Design and Implementation build the solution. Verification gives the verification.
  • Feedback. Maintenance starts new changes in Development: incidents, technical debt, and findings.
  • Explorer. The knowledge explorer reads this table. Keep its anchor and its columns. The row that links to the change flow is the phase that holds the steps. Page rules
  • Skills. The first skills cover Foundation, the steps of one change, and the wiki operations. Release and Maintenance skills come later. See PLAN.md.

The phases follow current AI SDLC methods: most start with a foundation step and loop back from operation to development. AWS AI-DLC, AI-SDLC (arXiv), Böckeler on SDD tools

Project knowledge

Document templates

Templates give consistent documents. The first one is the spec. Each template applies the rules of the method pages of this wiki. We test it on a real change in this repository (dogfooding rules). See the documentation catalog.

Each template states:

  • when to use it,
  • required sections and metadata (with a document ID where it applies).

Skills choose and fill the template. Scripts do the deterministic steps, such as assigning IDs or validating fields.

Knowledge wiki

A persistent wiki of linked Markdown pages for people and agents: a second brain for all the project documentation. AIDDbot keeps its own documents in one, and its skills help teams keep one in their projects. It is based on Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern. See the knowledge wiki page.

  • Keep original sources. Link every summary back to its evidence.
  • Agents add new sources, answer with references, and flag stale claims, contradictions, and broken links.
  • Files stay plain Markdown, usable in any editor.

Visual identity

AIDDbot documents and diagrams use the colors, fonts, and Mermaid rules in DESIGN.md.

Building blocks

BlockRoleRelations
SkillsRun development activities and handoffs, and generate documents. Each one defines: objective, needed context, standards, deliverables, and evidence of completion. The model chooses the approach. SkillTemplates, Scripts, Wiki, Foundation, Analysis, Design, Implementation, Verification, Close
TemplatesGive consistent documents. Skills choose and fill them. Document templatesspec, feature-file, review-report, adr
ScriptsDo deterministic tasks (Git chores, document IDs, metadata checks). Clear inputs, outputs, and error messages. They do not depend on the project stack or build tool. Skills do not repeat their logic in prose. ScriptVerification, Close, spec, wiki-page
WikiKeeps what the project knows now, linked to its sources. Knowledge wikiFoundation, Close, wiki-page, glossary
DistributionOne versioned release of the skills, templates, and CLI. The installer installs and updates it in a project. Only these three parts ship. What shipsSkills, Templates, Scripts, Foundation
Project contextGives repo conventions, commands, and constraints in AGENTS.md. Workflows use existing project tools and state their prerequisites. Project contextFoundation, agents, readme
  • Relations names other blocks, lifecycle phases, change steps, and document IDs in backticks.
  • The details of Templates and Wiki are in Project knowledge.
  • The knowledge explorer reads this table. Keep its anchor and its columns. Page rules

Shared core

The same core works in every AI coding tool:

  • the project context in AGENTS.md,
  • skills in the Agent Skills format,
  • the aiddbot CLI, when it is needed.

There is no CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules, or other file for one tool. Only the location of a skill and the way to load it can change between tools. The README documents them.

Hooks and tool integrations are optional and come later. See the future ideas.

Inclusion criteria

A skill or script belongs in AIDDbot only if it:

  1. solves a recurring need,
  2. adapts to different projects,
  3. produces a verifiable result,
  4. works on its own, with explicit inputs and outputs for handoffs,
  5. marks the decisions that need human approval and shows the evidence for them.

Decisions

#QuestionDecisionReason
1How are the lifecycle phases named?One word each: Foundation, Development, Release, Maintenance. Development holds the changes. Each change has five steps: Analysis, Design, Implementation, Verification, Close. It replaces the seven phases.With the project brain, Analysis and Design are change work only. Phase and step are two separate words, and each name shows once. "Development" is the classic SDLC word for this work.
2Is there a phase before Analysis?Yes: Foundation. It prepares the project set and the wiki.Most AI SDLC methods start with one (constitution, steering, bootstrap). "Context" clashes with the LLM term.
3How many levels of work?Two loops. The project loop has the four phases. The change loop has the five steps, inside Development. A phase is project level. A step is change level. The project documents of Analysis and Design go to the project brain.It separates the work on the whole project from the work on one change (audit item B3), with no name in both levels.
4Which phases get skills first?Foundation, the steps of one change, and the wiki operations. Release and Maintenance come later.They wait for a real need.
5Does Maintenance feed Development?Yes. Incidents, debt, and findings start new changes. No skill for it yet.Operational feedback starts a new iteration in current AI SDLC methods.
6Which blocks does the building blocks table list?Skills, Templates, Scripts, Wiki, Distribution, and Project context, with a Relations column.The knowledge explorer draws each block and its relations. Templates and Wiki were only detail sections.
7What do Implementation and Verification check?Implementation runs the deterministic quality checks: format, lint, and unit tests. Verification runs the end-to-end tests and an agent review of the diff against the review gates.The quality checks look at the code. Verification looks at the behavior and at what tests cannot see.
8How does the map show the two levels of work?Two loops. The project loop shows the four phases, with feedback from Maintenance to Development. The change loop is a zoom of Development with the five steps. Project documents go with the project loop. Change documents go with the change loop.The old map showed four names twice. Its arrow from Verification to Release said that every change makes a release. Its columns mixed project documents and change documents.
9How do Close and Release relate?Close is the last step of one change: the spec goes to done, durable knowledge goes back to the brain, and an entry goes to Unreleased in the changelog. Release is a project phase: it groups N closed changes into one version.Many changes close before one release.
10Where do the project documents of Analysis and Design go?To the project brain: one band of LIVE project documents between the two loops. Foundation creates the first ones. Each change reads them in Analysis and Design. Close updates them.Close already returns durable knowledge to the project documents. The brain makes that loop visible.
11What columns does the lifecycle phases table have?#, Phase, Work, Uses, Produces: the same columns as the change flow table. The Development row links to the change flow and lists no documents.One table shape for phases and steps. The explorer reads both with the same code. The documents of a change are in the change flow only.
12Which documents does the project brain show?Every document type of the document catalog with Life LIVE and Form DOC, in catalog order.No new list to maintain. Code and tests are living, but they are not project knowledge for the map.
13How does the catalog mark code and tests?A third tag, Form: DOC for text that people and agents read, and CODE for source code and tests that tools run.It follows the tag model of Life and Relevance. The explorer needs no hard-coded IDs. A new value comes with a real need.
14How does the map draw the path from Close to Release?Through the brain, with no new element. Close writes to the changelog, in its Unreleased section. Release reads the changelog and makes the version.Unreleased is a part of the changelog, not a new element. All knowledge flows through the brain in the same way.
15How does the map show Release and Maintenance?Like the other phases, with no "later" mark. Maintenance has no documents yet. Its dashed feedback arrow goes to Development.The map shows the method, not the state of the plan. PLAN.md holds the state.
16What is the name of the band of living project documents?The project brain. It holds every LIVE DOC document type. The knowledge wiki is one part of it. It replaces "project brain"."Brain" was the first wish for the wiki. With one name for the whole set, "brain" has one meaning.
17What does Analysis use and change in the project brain?It reads the roadmap, glossary, wiki-page, domain-model, adr, and agents. It writes the spec and the feature-file, and updates the roadmap. Close harvests the rest. Catalog decision 55Analysis needs the whole brain to frame the problem. Spec-first: other knowledge waits for Close.

Pending

No proposals are pending. Brainstorm proposals go here until they become rules.

docs.title: AIDDbot Knowledge Wiki
docs.html:
AIDDbot Knowledge Wiki

The wiki is the living knowledge of a project, for people and agents. It is a second brain for all the project documentation. AIDDbot uses it for its own documents, and its skills help teams keep one in their projects. Agents keep it up to date from sources. It follows Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern. See the intent and the documentation catalog.

Status: draft.

Model

Three layers:

LayerWhatRule
SourcesClosed specs and reports, ADRs, issues, pull requests, raw files, external URLs. SourcesNever edited by the wiki. Cited by the wiki.
WikiSynthesis pages: what the project knows now.Maintained by agents. Every claim cites a source.
SchemaThe wiki rules in this document.Tells agents how to ingest, answer, and review.

The wiki synthesizes; it does not copy. One fact has one home.

What is a wiki page

A wiki page is a prose LIVE document about one topic.

These LIVE documents stay outside the wiki, because tools or conventions need them in a fixed place. The wiki links to them:

DocumentWhy outside
agents, readme, changelogFixed names at the repository root.
design-systemLives with the UI code or in a shared guide. AIDDbot uses DESIGN.md at the repository root.
adrImmutable record; a source, not a synthesis.
roadmapFixed place at the repository root, next to the readme.

Repository layout

<project-root>/
├── AGENTS.md            # points agents to docs/wiki/index.md
└── docs/
    ├── wiki/
    │   ├── index.md     # catalog of pages
    │   └── <topic>.md
    ├── specs/           # one folder per change: spec and other change documents (sources)
    ├── adr/             # ADRs (sources)
    └── raw/             # imported files: transcripts, notes, articles (sources)

Git records the history of the wiki.

Page rules

  • Flat folder. All pages live in docs/wiki/. Add subfolders only when the index becomes hard to read.
  • Metadata. Each page starts with META frontmatter. A wiki page's id is its file name without .md (for example, glossary), because there is only one page per topic.
  • Synthesis first. The page starts with a short summary of the current state. Details follow.
  • Citations. Every claim links to its source with a relative Markdown link. A claim without a source is marked (unverified).
  • Conflicts. When sources disagree, the page shows both with their citations under a > [!warning] Conflict callout. A person decides.
  • Links. Use only standard relative Markdown links, such as [Glossary](glossary.md).
  • Explorer tables. The knowledge explorer reads seven tables: the lifecycle phases, the change flow, the impact levels, the building blocks, the document catalog, the Form tag, and the status use. Keep their headings and column names. Write document IDs in backticks. A change to them needs an explorer update. Explorer development

index.md

One line per page, grouped by type:

## Domain
- [Glossary](glossary.md) — shared terms for people, agents, and code

Agents read the index first. Then they open only the pages they need.

Operations

1. Ingest a source

A person or an agent gives a source: for example, a closed spec, an ADR, an issue, a pull request, or a file from docs/raw/.

  1. Read the source. See the source types.
  2. Find related pages in index.md.
  3. Update those pages, or create new ones, with citations.
  4. Mark conflicts with existing claims.
  5. Update index.md.

2. Answer a question

  1. Read index.md, then the relevant pages.
  2. Check the original sources where needed.
  3. Answer with citations. State uncertainty.
  4. If the answer adds knowledge, offer to save it as a page.

3. Review the wiki

Check, then fix what the sources support. Flag the rest for a person.

  • Claims with no source, or with sources that no longer say it.
  • Conflicts between pages.
  • Pages missing from index.md, and orphan pages.
  • Broken links and invalid META.

Sources

SourceWhere it livesHow the wiki cites it
Closed specs, plans, and review reportsdocs/specs/Relative link.
ADRsdocs/adr/Relative link.
Issues and pull requestsThe issue tracker or the Git hostURL.
Incident reports and postmortemsThe project documents or the incident toolRelative link or URL.
Transcripts, meeting notes, articlesdocs/raw/Relative link.
External referencesThe webURL.

Ingest only sources with durable knowledge, such as the cause of a defect or a decision taken in a pull request. Not every issue or pull request needs an ingest.

  • docs/raw/ is immutable. Files are added, never edited or deleted.
  • Cite project documents in place. Do not copy them to docs/raw/.
  • Cite issues, pull requests, and external references by URL. Save a local copy only when the page may change or disappear; record the original URL and capture date in its frontmatter.

Access

  • Agents: agents says: "For project knowledge, start at docs/wiki/index.md."
  • People: any Markdown editor. On GitHub, links work as they are.

Obsidian

Obsidian can open the repository as a vault. It reads the pages, the relative links, the META frontmatter as properties, Mermaid diagrams, and callouts.

Set these options in Settings → Files & links, so that new links stay standard Markdown:

OptionValue
Use [[Wikilinks]]Off
New link formatRelative path to file

Known limits:

  • Links to an anchor, such as glossary.md#spec, open the page but do not go to the section. Obsidian does not use GitHub heading anchors or HTML <a id> anchors.
  • File names in the links field of META do not show in the graph. Obsidian shows only [[...]] links there.

Do not use [[...]] links in pages. GitHub and other editors do not read them.

Deferred

These ideas wait for a real need.

  • A log.md of wiki operations. Git is the history.
  • Automatic ingest when a change closes.

docs.title: AIDDbot Scaffolding
docs.html:
AIDDbot Scaffolding

Status: draft.

This page states where AIDDbot keeps its files. Create each folder only when the work needs it. The project plan sets the order.

Layout

aidd-bot/
├── AGENTS.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE
├── PLAN.md                         # Roadmap: milestones and tasks
├── DESIGN.md                       # Design system
├── package.json                    # Private repository manifest
├── docs/
│   ├── wiki/                       # The AIDDbot wiki: index.md and pages
│   └── specs/                      # One folder per change: spec, feature files, plan, review
├── templates/                      # Shared document templates
├── skills/
│   └── <skill-name>/SKILL.md       # Shared skill source
└── packages/
    ├── cli/                        # The aiddbot CLI
    └── explorer/                   # The knowledge explorer (does not ship)

What ships

AIDDbot is a help for development teams that use AI across the software lifecycle. A release gives them only these parts:

ShipsSource
Skillsskills/
Document templatestemplates/
AIDDbot CLIpackages/cli/

Everything else stays in this repository: the roadmap, the specs, the AIDDbot wiki, and the knowledge explorer. They are how we build AIDDbot, not what teams install.

When each folder appears

FolderCreated whenMilestone
docs/specs/The first spec is written.H1
templates/The first template is written: the spec.H2
skills/The first skill is written: the Analysis step of a change.H2
packages/cli/The first CLI command is written.H3
packages/explorer/The knowledge explorer is built: s0002.H1
docs/adr/The first ADR is written.When needed
docs/wiki/The foundational documents become the AIDDbot wiki.H1
docs/raw/The wiki ingests the first external source.When needed

Configure the Bun workspace when a second package exists. Until then, the root scripts run the explorer with --cwd. Explorer development

Skills and templates

  • Keep one source folder per skill in skills/. Put the entry point in SKILL.md. Use references/ and assets/ for resources that travel with that skill. Agent Skills specification
  • Keep shared document templates in templates/. A skill that needs a template references it. Do not copy its content into the skill.
  • The same skill works in every AI coding tool. Until the installer exists, copy it by hand to the location that each tool supports. The README.md documents the location and the way to load the skill in each tool.
  • Keep the source in skills/ only. Do not commit copies in tool folders. Do not add CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules, or other files for one tool.

docs.title: Build the AIDDbot wiki from the foundational documents
docs.html:
s0001 · Build the AIDDbot wiki from the foundational documents

Goal

The foundational documents hold the AIDDbot design. Today they sit at the repository root, without META, and they mix two audiences:

  • the method that AIDDbot gives to teams through its skills and templates,
  • the way we build AIDDbot.

An audit before this spec found contradictions, gaps, and overlaps between them. This change turns the documents into the AIDDbot knowledge wiki and fixes the audit items. The wiki is the base for the skill map and the H2 skills. H1

This is also the first spec of AIDDbot. A person writes it by hand, to test the spec format.

Scope

In

1. Pages. Move the documents to docs/wiki/ with lowercase names. Group them in index.md:

GroupPageFrom
About AIDDbotintent.mdINTENT.md
About AIDDbotglossary.mdGLOSSARY.md
Methoddocumentation-catalog.mdDOCUMENTATION-CATALOG.md
Methodknowledge-wiki.mdKNOWLEDGE-WIKI.md
Methodaiddbot-cli.mdSCRIPT-TOOLCHAIN.md: prerequisite, execution from skills, script contract, candidate commands.
Developmentcli-development.mdSCRIPT-TOOLCHAIN.md: runtime, development commands, packaging, test before the first publish.
Developmentscaffolding.mdSCAFFOLDING.md
  • Method pages hold the rules that AIDDbot ships to teams through its skills and templates.
  • Development pages hold the rules to build AIDDbot. They do not ship.
  • AGENTS.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, PLAN.md, DESIGN.md, and LICENSE stay at the root. index.md links to them.

2. Audit fixes.

#ProblemFix
A1The catalog says that every document starts with META. Only two documents have it.Every wiki page, PLAN.md, and every spec has META. AGENTS.md, README.md, and CHANGELOG.md are exempt: tools read them at fixed names. The catalog states the exemption.
A2The catalog keeps the old rule "only the documents that the next real change needs".The catalog defines the documents that the skill map needs. Update its status line and decision 18.
A3META validation is a future idea and also a candidate command.It is a candidate command for H3 only. Remove it from the future ideas and from the deferred wiki ideas.
A4Scaffolding says that skills are copied by hand. H4 plans an installer.Skills are copied by hand until the H4 installer exists.
A5META has one date field: the last status change. It does not show when the content changed.Replace date with created (never changes) and updated (last content change). Both are ISO 8601 dates, without time. Git keeps the status history. Update decision 4.
B1Method rules mention AIDDbot internals: dogfooding, PLAN.md, "people who use AIDDbot".Method pages do not use the term dogfooding and do not link to PLAN.md or to development pages. The spec Findings section becomes "lessons about the way of working".
B2PLAN.md has no document type.Add the roadmap type to the catalog: LIVE, COULD, milestones and their tasks. PLAN.md uses it.
C1The change flow is repeated in README.md, AGENTS.md, the catalog, and the glossary.The catalog holds the flow. The other documents keep a short summary and link to it.
C2"Script" names both a CLI command and the H4 installer.Add the term installer to the glossary. PLAN.md uses it.
C3PLAN.md says "review" for the wiki review.Write "wiki review".
D1Anchor links do not go to the section in Obsidian.Keep the anchor links. GitHub is the main reader. knowledge-wiki.md already states the limit. Close the H1 task about anchors.
D2The DESIGN.md ID design-system-0001 does not follow the ID rules.The ID is design-system. The catalog states the rule: one per project.
D3AGENTS.md does not point agents to the wiki.AGENTS.md says: "For project knowledge, start at docs/wiki/index.md." Its reference table uses the new paths.

3. Related updates. Update every link, SCAFFOLDING layout, the AGENTS.md rule about foundational documents, and CHANGELOG.md. Ignore the .obsidian/ settings folder in .gitignore: it is local, and it belongs to one tool. Added during the review, for check 8.

Out

  • The skill map and audit items B3 and B4: the relation between the change flow and the lifecycle stages, and the documents for release and operation. A later H1 change does them.
  • New rules or new content, except the META dates of A5. This change moves, splits, and fixes. It does not redesign.
  • Templates, skills, and CLI code.

Acceptance

#CriterionCheck
1docs/wiki/ holds index.md and the seven pages of the scope. The root holds no other foundational document.List the files.
2Every wiki page, PLAN.md, DESIGN.md, and this spec start with valid META, with created and updated and without date. A wiki page id equals its file name without .md.Script: parse the frontmatter, check the required fields and the id rule.
3No relative link or anchor is broken.Script: resolve every relative link and its anchor.
4index.md lists each page once, under its group, with a one-line summary.Review.
5Method pages do not contain the term dogfooding and do not link to PLAN.md or to development pages.Search the Method pages.
6Each audit item of the scope has its fix.Review each row of the audit table.
7No rule is lost in the move.Review the Git diff: each removed line is moved or has a reason.
8A person opens the repository in Obsidian with the documented settings. The pages, links, and META properties work, within the known limits.Manual review.

Tasks

  • Create docs/wiki/ and move the documents with git mv, to keep their history.
  • Split SCRIPT-TOOLCHAIN.md into aiddbot-cli.md and cli-development.md.
  • Add META to each page and to PLAN.md. Fix the DESIGN.md ID.
  • Apply the audit fixes.
  • Write index.md.
  • Update AGENTS.md, README.md, SCAFFOLDING layout, every link, and CHANGELOG.md.
  • Run the checks and record the evidence.
  • A person reviews the result in GitHub and Obsidian.

Verification

Checks run on 2026-11-24 with a temporary script, check_s0001.py, outside the repository. It checks the files, META, every relative link and anchor, and the Method pages.

#ResultEvidence
1Passdocs/wiki/: index.md and the seven pages. Root: AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, DESIGN.md, PLAN.md, README.md.
2Pass11 documents checked: required fields, no date, wiki page id equals the file name, DESIGN.md ID is design-system.
3Pass115 relative links checked. None broken.
4Passindex.md lists the seven pages once, in the About, Method, and Development groups. It also lists the documents outside the wiki. A person reviewed it.
5PassNo dogfood, no link to PLAN.md, scaffolding.md, or cli-development.md in the Method pages.
6PassEach row A1 to D3 has its fix. A person reviewed it.
7PassEach removed line in git diff --cached -M is a moved line, a new link path, or an audit fix. A person reviewed it.
8PassA person opened the repository root as an Obsidian vault with the documented settings. Links and META properties work.

Findings

  • The audit made the scope clear. A read-only audit before the spec gave a numbered list of problems. The spec reused it as its scope. A future skill can start a documentation change with an audit.
  • The checks are repeated work. The link and META checks ran twice, before and after the change, with throwaway scripts. They are the first input for doc validate in H3.
  • The scope changed at approval. The person added the META dates (A5) while reviewing the spec. The spec template needs a simple way to record changes made at approval.
  • The spec linked to paths that did not exist yet. Its links to docs/wiki/ broke until the implementation. The link check must skip or flag specs in draft and accepted status.

Findings

#FindingProposal
1bun lint does not exist in Bun 1.4.5. AGENTS.md, cli-development.md, and s0002 ask for it.A person chooses a linter, or waits for the Bun linter. Then update the three documents.
2The spec named four chapter tables. The builder needs a fifth: the status use table, for the document type diagram.Recorded in the wiki contract. No action.
3The Set in column of the status use has one value for all document types. draft says "Foundation, Analysis", but a spec is drafted only in Analysis.Decide in the skill map if Set in needs one row for each document group.
4The block diagram needs block-to-block links ("Skills uses Templates"). The spec gave only one new column. The Relations column now holds block names too.Recorded in the wiki contract. No action.
5The Claude in Chrome extension was not connected. Headless Chrome with the DevTools protocol checked the clicks, the zoom, and reduced motion instead.A future end-to-end test can reuse this approach.
6The explorer is the first package, but there is no Bun workspace. A new clone must run bun run explorer:install before the build.Configure the workspace with the second package, as scaffolding says.
7The logo loads from the author's site. Offline, the header has no icon.Decide with the open question about the AIDDbot logo in DESIGN.md.
8The mermaid package adds about 100 chunk files to the build output. It loads only for documents with Mermaid blocks.No action while the site is local. Check again before a public host.

Decisions taken during the implementation

These choices were not in the spec. A person reviews them.

  • The building blocks table keeps Project context and adds Templates and Wiki: six blocks.
  • The Foundation row names readme and wiki-page in backticks, so they hang under Foundation on the map.
  • A document type hangs under the first phase that names it. Only if no phase names it, it hangs under the first step that produces it.
  • After accepted, the later statuses branch, so an adr ends as superseded or deprecated.
  • Fonts use only the Latin subsets, and the bundler puts them inside styles.css.
  • The element views use the attributes element and doc, not id, so they do not clash with heading anchors.

docs.title: Build the web knowledge explorer
docs.html:
s0002 - Build the web knowledge explorer

Problem

Goal

The AIDDbot knowledge lives in Markdown files: the wiki, the root documents, and the specs. GitHub and Obsidian show them as separate plain pages. A person cannot see the whole method at once: the lifecycle phases, the steps of a change, the building blocks, and the documents that each step makes.

This change builds a web explorer that tells the story of AIDDbot to people, as visually as possible. A map shows the whole method. Each part of the method has its own page with an animated diagram. The full documents are one click away. The explorer is documentation for people. It is not a graph viewer and not a copy of Obsidian.

It is part of the Foundation phase: it makes the project knowledge easy to understand before we design the skills and templates. Lifecycle phases

Out of scope

  • Publication to a public host, such as GitHub Pages.
  • Search, editing, comments, and authentication.
  • A graph of all the documents and their links.
  • Reuse for the wiki of other projects, and any change to what ships. A later spec can do it.
  • Validation of documents. The doc validate command of H3 does it. The explorer only shows the problems that it finds while it reads.
  • Links to files outside the content scope, such as LICENSE, on a Git host. The repository has no remote yet.

User stories

  • US1 - As a person who learns AIDDbot, I want one visual map of the whole method, so that I see how its phases, steps, building blocks, and documents fit together.
  • US2 - As a person who studies one part of AIDDbot, I want a page for that part with an animated diagram and its details, so that I understand it without reading the whole wiki.
  • US3 - As a person who wants all the details, I want to read the full documents rendered with their metadata and working links, so that I go deeper from any page.

Solution

How it works

The explorer has two parts: a builder that reads the documents, and a site that shows them in the browser.

graph LR
  Wiki[Wiki tables and sections] -->|read| Builder[Builder]
  Docs[Full documents] -->|read| Builder
  Design[DESIGN.md] -->|colors and fonts| Builder
  Builder -->|writes| Site[Static site]
  Site -->|opens in| Browser[Browser]

Text equivalent: the builder reads the wiki tables and sections, the full documents, and DESIGN.md. It writes a static site. A person opens the site in a browser.

  1. The builder runs on the person's machine with Bun. It reads four chapter tables from the wiki, the wiki sections and glossary terms that their rows link to, and every document of the content scope with its META. It writes one data file and copies the site files next to it. It stops with a clear error when the wiki breaks the contract below. It lists each smaller problem: a missing META, an invalid META, or a broken link.
  2. The site is a set of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files. It works on any static file server, also in a subfolder, because all its paths are relative and the views use hash addresses, such as #/phase/design. It loads the data file and shows the view that the address asks for.

The wiki stays the single source of truth. The site adds only layout and animation. It never edits a document.

Chapters

The explorer tells AIDDbot in four chapters. Each chapter comes from one table of the wiki. Each row of the table is one element of the method.

ChapterElementSource tableColumns
Lifecycle phasesPhaseintent.md#lifecycle-phases#, Phase, AIDDbot helps teams to, Project level, Change level (as today)
Change flowStepdocumentation-catalog.md#change-flow#, Step, Work, Uses, Produces (new table)
Building blocksBlockintent.md#building-blocksBlock, Role, and a new column with the phases or documents that the block touches
DocumentsDocument typedocumentation-catalog.md#document-catalogID, Document, Life, Relevance, Standards, Purpose (as today)

Wiki contract

The builder and the wiki agree on a small contract:

  • Location. The builder finds each chapter by its fixed anchor, and reads the first table under it. The column names are fixed.
  • Links between elements. A document ID in backticks, such as `spec`, links to that document type. A step with the same name as a phase links to that phase.
  • Errors. A missing anchor, a renamed column, or an unknown document ID stops the build. The error names the file and the problem.
  • Rule for editors. The page rules of knowledge-wiki.md say that these anchors and columns are stable. A change to them needs an explorer update. The details are in explorer-development.md.

To meet the contract, the wiki changes in four places:

PageChange
documentation-catalog.mdThe change flow becomes a table with Uses and Produces.
documentation-catalog.md"Status use" becomes a table: Status, Meaning, Set in step, and a column that says which document types use it. Life is not enough, because adr is LIVE with its own cycle.
intent.mdThe building blocks table adds Templates and Wiki, and the new column. "Project knowledge" keeps its detail sections, and the rows link to them.
knowledge-wiki.mdThe page rules add the contract rule.

Views

ViewAddressUser storyContent
Map#/US1The home view. One picture in layers, described below.
Element page#/<kind>/<id>US2The row as a summary, the animated diagram of its kind, the wiki sections and glossary terms that the row links to, and the mini-map. A document type page also lists the documents of the content scope of that type.
Full document#/doc/<id>US3The rendered Markdown, the META fields as badges, a table of contents, and the related documents and sources as links.
Not foundany otherUS1A message and a link to the map.

The map

The map is one picture in layers:

        ┌──────── Maintenance ◄── Release ◄──┐
        │                                     │
        ▼     ┌─── change flow ──────────┐    │
  Foundation ─► Analysis ► Design ► Impl ► Verif ► Close
   [glossary]   [spec]     [adr]           [review-report]

 ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Skills · Templates · Scripts · Wiki · Distribution
  • The phase loop is in the middle. The change flow sits inside the change-level phases. The document types hang under the phase or step that names them. The building blocks form a band below.
  • Code places each element by rules, from the table order. Nobody draws the map by hand. A new table row appears on the map with no drawing work.
  • A click on an element zooms the map into it, and then opens its page.
  • The same picture, small, is the mini-map of each page. It marks the current element. A click on the mini-map goes back to the map.

Page diagrams

Each element kind has one diagram template. The builder fills it from the tables, so a new row gets its diagram with no drawing work. The diagram builds up step by step when the page opens.

PHASE  (Design)
  Analysis ──► [ Design ] ──► Implementation
                  │
       project: adr, design-system
       change:  tasks / impl-plan

STEP   (Verification)
  spec ──► [ Verification ] ──► ticked spec
                  └── fails? ─► review-report

BLOCK  (Skills)
  [ Skills ] ── uses ──► Templates, Scripts
      └── runs in ──► Analysis … Close

DOCUMENT  (spec)
  draft ──► accepted ──► done
   Analysis   Design      Close

Content

GroupFilesShown as
Wikidocs/wiki/*.mdChapter tables, linked sections, and full documents
RootREADME.md, AGENTS.md, PLAN.md, DESIGN.md, CHANGELOG.mdFull documents
Specsdocs/specs/*.mdFull documents

Rules for META:

  • Wiki pages and specs must have META. If it is missing or invalid, the document shows a warning.
  • README.md, AGENTS.md, and CHANGELOG.md have no META by design. They show no warning. The builder gives them their document type from the file name: readme, agent-instructions, and changelog.
  • DESIGN.md keeps its META under the aiddbot key of its frontmatter, as the DESIGN.md format asks.
  • A link to a file outside the content scope, such as LICENSE, shows as plain text with a small "outside the explorer" mark.

Building blocks

  • Web Components. Each part of the screen is one custom element in its own file, such as <aidd-map>, <element-page>, or <doc-view>. A component can be reused in any view. There is no UI framework.
  • Visual identity. The colors of DESIGN.md become CSS variables. The dark theme is the default. A button switches to the light theme. The three fonts come from @fontsource packages and ship with the site.
  • Animations. The map, the page diagrams, and the zoom are hand-written SVG and CSS, with the Web Animations API. When the browser asks for reduced motion, every diagram shows its final state at once, and a click opens the page with no zoom.
  • Libraries. Only two:
    • The builder parses Markdown with the built-in Bun.markdown. It adds heading ids as GitHub slugs, because Bun.markdown does not.
    • The mermaid package renders the Mermaid blocks of a full document, with the colors of DESIGN.md. The site loads it only when such a document opens. The map and the element pages never load it.
    • Each library is pinned in package.json.
  • Language and checks. TypeScript on Bun, as in CLI development. bun lint, bunx tsc --noEmit, and bun test run on the explorer code.

Repository changes

  • Code in packages/explorer/, the first package of the repository. The build output is ignored by Git.
  • Root package.json scripts: explorer:dev (a local server that rebuilds on change) and explorer:build.
  • The four wiki changes of the wiki contract.
  • A new Development wiki page, explorer-development.md: commands, folders, the wiki contract in detail, and the component rules. index.md lists it.
  • Updates to scaffolding.md, AGENTS.md (the checks apply to the explorer code), PLAN.md, the glossary (term knowledge explorer), and CHANGELOG.md.

Tasks

  • Change the wiki tables and add the contract rule, as the wiki contract says. Check: no broken link.
  • Create packages/explorer/ with its package.json, TypeScript settings, and the root scripts. Check: bun run explorer:build runs.
  • Write the reader: chapter tables, links between elements, linked sections, documents, and META, with unit tests. Check: bun test, and US1R4 with a broken copy of the wiki.
  • Write the site shell, the router, the theme, and the not-found view. Check: US1R1, and an unknown address shows the not-found view.
  • Write the map. Check: US1R2, US1R3.
  • Write the element pages and the four diagram templates. Check: US2R1.
  • Write the full document view. Check: US3R1, US3R2.
  • Apply the visual identity and the reduced motion rule. Check: US2R2, US2R3.
  • Update the documents of "Repository changes". Check: no broken link.
  • Check each requirement and tick it. Write the review report only if a requirement fails or there are findings.

Verification

  • US1R1 - When a person runs the build script, the explorer shall write a static site that works from a subfolder of a static file server.
  • US1R2 - When a person opens the map, the explorer shall show every phase, step, building block, and document type of the chapter tables, in their table order, with the links between them.
  • US1R3 - When a person clicks an element on the map, the explorer shall zoom into that element and then open its page.
  • US1R4 - If a chapter anchor, a chapter column, or a document ID of the wiki contract is missing or unknown, then the build shall stop with an error that names the file and the problem.
  • US2R1 - When a person opens an element page, the explorer shall show the row summary, the animated diagram of the element kind, the linked wiki sections and glossary terms, and the mini-map with the element marked.
  • US2R2 - The explorer shall use the colors and fonts of DESIGN.md, with a dark and a light theme, and a text contrast of at least 4.5:1.
  • US2R3 - While the browser asks for reduced motion, the explorer shall show every diagram in its final state and open pages with no zoom.
  • US3R1 - When a person opens a full document, the explorer shall render its headings, tables, code blocks, and Mermaid diagrams, show its META fields as badges, and open each relative link to a document of the content scope at its target anchor.
  • US3R2 - If a wiki page or a spec has no META or an invalid META, or a document has a broken relative link, then the explorer shall show the document with a warning, and the build shall list each problem with its file.

docs.html:
s0003 - Separate the project loop and the change loop

Problem

Goal

The lifecycle model mixes two levels of work. The lifecycle phases table has seven phases. Four of them (Analysis, Design, Implementation, Verification) are also steps of the change flow. The explorer map shows the same four names twice, in two rows.

The map has three more problems:

  • An arrow goes from Verification to Release. It says that every change makes a release. In fact, many changes close before one release.
  • The document columns mix project documents (roadmap, adr) with change documents (spec, impl-plan).
  • Close and Release look unrelated. In fact, Close fills the Unreleased section of the changelog, and Release reads it.

This change applies the brainstorm proposals P1 to P9 in the Pending section of intent.md: a project loop with four phases, a change loop with five steps, and a knowledge shelf between them.

Out of scope

  • Skills, templates, and scripts for Release and Maintenance.
  • New document types for Maintenance, such as incidents or technical debt.
  • A new layout for the building blocks band. It stays as it is.
  • Changes to the element page diagrams of steps, blocks, and document types.

User stories

  • US1 - As a person who learns AIDDbot, I want the map to show the project loop and the change loop apart, with the knowledge shelf between them, so that I see each phase and step once and how closed changes reach a release.
  • US2 - As a person who edits the wiki, I want the lifecycle model and the document catalog to hold the new model in their tables, so that the explorer and the future skills read one model from one place.

Solution

The model

graph LR
  Foundation --> Development --> Release --> Maintenance
  Maintenance -.->|incidents, debt, findings| Development
  subgraph Change[One change, inside Development]
    Analysis --> Design --> Implementation --> Verification --> Close
  end
  Close -->|writes Unreleased| Changelog[changelog]
  Changelog -->|reads| Release

Text equivalent: the project has four phases: Foundation, Development, Release, and Maintenance. Maintenance feeds new changes back to Development. Development holds the changes. Each change has five steps: Analysis, Design, Implementation, Verification, and Close. Close writes to the Unreleased section of the changelog. Release reads the changelog and makes a version.

  • A phase is project level. A step is change level. Each name is used once.
  • The knowledge shelf holds the LIVE project documents. Foundation creates the first ones. Each change reads them in Analysis and Design. Close updates them.

Wiki changes

PageChangeProposal
intent.mdThe lifecycle phases table gets four rows and the columns #, Phase, Work, Uses, Produces. The Development row links to the change flow and lists no documents. The notes below the table follow the new model.P1, P4, P5
intent.mdThe decisions table replaces decisions 1 and 3, and adds the decisions of P1 to P9. The Pending section goes away.All
documentation-catalog.mdThe Tags section adds a third tag, Form: DOC (text for people and agents) and CODE (source code and tests that tools run). The document catalog adds a Form column after Life.P7
documentation-catalog.mdThe change flow intro no longer says that its steps use the names of the phases. It says that the change flow is the work of the Development phase. Close a change says that the changelog entry goes to Unreleased.P2, P4
glossary.mdNew term: Development. Changed terms: lifecycle phase, project level, change level, close. New term: knowledge shelf.P3, P4
explorer-development.mdThe wiki contract gets the new columns of two tables. The map rules describe the two loops and the shelf.P1, P5, P6, P8
Other pagesThe pages that name seven phases or the Project level and Change level columns follow the new model: README.md, AGENTS.md, PLAN.md, scaffolding.md, index.md.P4

Builder changes

  • Phases table. The builder reads the new columns. The ID columns are now Uses and Produces, as in the change flow table. The same code reads both tables.
  • Form. The builder reads the Form column of the catalog. An unknown value stops the build.
  • Steps and phases. A step no longer links to a phase with the same name. All steps link to the phase whose row links to the change flow: Development. No phase name is written in the code.
  • Shelf. The shelf holds every document type with LIVE and DOC, in catalog order. No document ID is written in the code.

The map

PROJECT    Foundation ──► Development ──► Release ──► Maintenance
                              ▲    │ zoom     ▲            │
                              └────┼──────────┼── feedback ┘
                                   │          │ reads
SHELF     │ readme  glossary  wiki-page  roadmap  adr  ...  changelog │
                                   │          ▲ writes
CHANGE     Analysis ► Design ► Implementation ► Verification ► Close
           spec       impl-plan code             test-report
                      feature-file unit-test     review-report

Map rules:

  • Project loop. The phases form the top row, in table order. A dashed arrow goes from the last phase to the phase that holds the change flow.
  • Change loop. The steps form the bottom row, in table order, inside a frame. A zoom line goes from Development to the frame.
  • Shelf. The shelf is a band between the two loops.
  • Document types. A shelf document type sits only on the shelf. Any other document type hangs under the first step that produces it, or else under the first step that uses it.
  • Links to the shelf. The map always draws the links between the phases and the shelf, and the links from Close to the shelf. For example, Close writes the changelog and Release reads it. The links of the other steps show when a person points at the step.
  • Phase page. The phase diagram shows Uses and Produces, as the step diagram does. The Development page also lists the five steps.

Tasks

  • Change the wiki tables and pages, as the wiki changes say. Check: US2R1, US2R2, and no broken link.
  • Change the builder: phases table, Form, steps and phases, shelf, with unit tests. Check: US2R3, bun test.
  • Change the map layout and the phase diagram. Check: US1R1 to US1R5.
  • Run bunx tsc --noEmit and bun test. Check: both pass.
  • Update CHANGELOG.md and PLAN.md. Check: no broken link.
  • Check each requirement and tick it. Write the review report only if a requirement fails or there are findings.

Verification

  • US1R1 - When a person opens the map, the explorer shall show the phases of the lifecycle phases table in one row, in table order, with a dashed feedback arrow from the last phase to the phase that holds the change flow.
  • US1R2 - When a person opens the map, the explorer shall show the steps of the change flow table in one framed row, in table order, linked to the phase that holds the change flow, and shall show each phase and step name once.
  • US1R3 - When a person opens the map, the explorer shall show a knowledge shelf with every document type with LIVE life and DOC form, in catalog order, and no other document type.
  • US1R4 - When a person opens the map, the explorer shall draw the links between the phases and the shelf documents, and the links from the last step to the shelf documents.
  • US1R5 - When a person opens the page of a phase, the explorer shall show its Uses and Produces documents, and, for the phase that holds the change flow, its steps.
  • US2R1 - The lifecycle phases table shall have the columns #, Phase, Work, Uses, and Produces, and the rows Foundation, Development, Release, and Maintenance.
  • US2R2 - The document catalog shall have a Form column after Life, with DOC or CODE in each row, and the Tags section shall define Form.
  • US2R3 - If the Form column is missing, or a row holds a Form value that the Tags section does not define, then the build shall stop with an error that names the file and the problem.

s0005 - Give the explorer maps in layers

Problem

Goal

The explorer map shows everything at once: the project loop, the project brain with all its document types, the document types under each step, the links, and the building blocks band. A person who opens the explorer for the first time sees too much. The building blocks add noise and no story to the map.

This change gives the information in layers. It applies the brainstorm proposals M1 to M7 of 2026-11-26:

#Proposal
M1Level 0 is an overview: phases, the project brain as one box, and the steps as boxes. No document types, no building blocks. A click opens a map with more detail. Element pages are the last level.
M2The building blocks leave the maps. They get the view #/blocks, with a link in the header.
M3The project brain has its own map.
M4The change loop has one map, with a filter of impact level.
M5The impact levels table gets the columns Skips and Adds. The wiki contract has seven tables.
M6Each map has an address. Each element has one parent map. The breadcrumbs show the full path.
M7The mini-map draws the parent map of the element.

Out of scope

  • New content for the element pages and their diagrams.
  • An impact filter on the overview or the brain map.
  • Changes to the building blocks table of the intent page.
  • A map with more detail for a phase.

User stories

  • US1 - As a person who learns AIDDbot, I want a short overview first and the building blocks apart, so that the first view does not overload me.
  • US2 - As a person who learns AIDDbot, I want a detail map of the change loop and of the project brain, and a filter by impact level, so that I see the documents only when I ask for them.
  • US3 - As a person who explores AIDDbot, I want breadcrumbs and a mini-map that show the map of each element, so that I always know where I am and how to go back.

Solution

Levels

graph TD
  L0["Level 0 · #/<br/>phases, brain box, step boxes"]
  L1a["Level 1 · #/map/change<br/>steps and their document types"]
  L1b["Level 1 · #/map/brain<br/>brain document types, who writes and reads them"]
  B["#/blocks<br/>building blocks"]
  P["Element pages<br/>#/phase, #/step, #/type, #/block"]
  L0 -->|click the change loop| L1a
  L0 -->|click the brain| L1b
  L0 -->|click a phase| P
  L1a --> P
  L1b --> P
  B --> P

Text equivalent: the overview at #/ opens the change loop map, the brain map, and the phase pages. The two detail maps open the step and document type pages. The blocks view at #/blocks opens the block pages.

Parent map

Each element has one parent map. The breadcrumbs and the mini-map use it.

ElementParent mapBreadcrumbs
PhaseOverview #/Map › Foundation
StepChange loop #/map/changeMap › Change loop › Design
Document type of the brainBrain #/map/brainMap › Project brain › glossary
Other document typeChange loop #/map/changeMap › Change loop › spec
Building blockBlocks #/blocksMap › Building blocks › Skills

The maps

LEVEL 0     Foundation ──► Development ──► Release ──► Maintenance
                               │ zoom          ▲            │
                               ▼               │  feedback  │
            ┌─ PROJECT BRAIN ──────────────────┴──┐ ◄───────┘
            └─────────────────────────────────────┘
            Analysis ► Design ► Implementation ► Verification ► Close

CHANGE      │ readme  glossary  wiki-page  agents  roadmap  adr  ... │
LOOP        Analysis ► Design ► Implementation ► Verification ► Close
            spec       ...       code             test-report
            [ small | medium | large ]

BRAIN       Foundation  Development  Release  Maintenance  (phases)
            │ readme  glossary  wiki-page  agents  roadmap  adr  ... │
            Analysis    Design   Implementation   Verification   Close

Map rules:

  • Overview. It keeps the project loop row, the zoom line, and the feedback arrow of today. The brain is one box with its name and the count of its document types. The steps are boxes in a frame, with no document types under them. A link joins a phase or a step to the brain box when its Uses or Produces holds a brain document type.
  • Clicks on the overview. A phase opens its page. The brain box opens the brain map. The change loop frame or a step opens the change loop map.
  • Change loop map. It is the current map without the project loop row and without the blocks band. The brain band stays above the steps. The rules for document types and links stay as they are.
  • Impact filter. The change loop map has a selector: small, medium, large. The default is medium. A level hides the document types in its Skips cell. It marks the document types in its Adds cell as required.
  • Brain map. The brain document types form the middle row, in catalog order. The phases form the top row, and the steps the bottom row. A person who points at a document type sees the links to the phases and steps that use or produce it. A person who points at a phase or a step sees its links.
  • Blocks view. It lists every building block in table order, with its role and a link to its page.

Wiki changes

PageChangeProposal
documentation-catalog.mdThe impact levels table gets the columns Skips and Adds, after Flow. small skips feature-file, e2e-test, and test-report. large adds review-report. medium holds — in both.M5
explorer-development.mdThe wiki contract gets the impact levels table: seven tables. The map rules and the site rules describe the levels, the addresses, the parent map, and the blocks view. The Pending section goes away.M1 to M7

s0006 - Publish the AIDDbot knowledge explorer

Problem

Goal

Publish the existing explorer as the public documentation for AIDDbot and its development process. Make this repository the official project and preserve the previous version as an archive.

User stories

  • US1 - As a person learning AIDDbot, I want to explore its method and development in a browser, so that I can see how the project applies its own method.

Solution

  1. Rename the previous repository to AIDDbot/AIDDbot-legacy. Publish this repository and its history as AIDDbot/AIDDbot and set the local origin to it.
  2. Use GitHub Actions to install the locked Bun dependencies, build the explorer, and publish packages/explorer/dist/ to GitHub Pages on pushes to main and manual runs on main. Link the public explorer from the README.
  3. After verifying the site, link the legacy README to the new repository and archive the legacy repository.

Verification

  • US1R1 - When a visitor opens https://aiddbot.github.io/AIDDbot/, the public explorer shall show the method overview and let the visitor open the project plan and a completed spec without signing in.
  • US1R2 - When a push reaches main or a maintainer runs the workflow manually on main, GitHub Actions shall build and publish the explorer after a successful build.
  • US1R3 - After the cutover, GitHub shall serve this project at AIDDbot/AIDDbot and the previous project as a public archive at AIDDbot/AIDDbot-legacy with a README link to the successor.
